case_name: Tara Bai Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Tara Bai Singh, widow of Late Shri Madan Chand Singh
parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Madhya Pradesh and others

facts_of_case: Petitioner is the widow of Late Shri Madan Chand Singh. She claims family pension on his death. Impugned orders denying her claim are challenged.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage is valid only when it is solemnized in accordance with the provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
legal_principles.held: Reading exhaustively from this judgment, specifically paragraphs 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23, it is submitted that amongst the Hindus, a marriage is a valid marriage only when it is solemnized in accordance with the provisions under section 5 and section 7 of the Act of 1955.
cited_cases: Union of India and others Vs. Padmini Dehuri, (2019) (3) MPLJ 215

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party claiming a valid remarriage to prove that it was solemnized in accordance with the provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
legal_principles.held: Thus, there being evidence of solemnization of remarriage, pension should be allowed and the impugned orders be quashed.

outcome.final_order: The writ petition is filed by the widow of Late Shri Madan Chand Singh being aggrieved of impugned orders denying her claim towards family pension on death of her husband.
